The action has been declared indefinite—until an acceptable solution is reached by Brussels. findings.title: Вдвое больше дорог для 35-метровых автопоездов: шведы довольны экспериментом с гигантскими фурами
findings.summary: Швеция расширяет дороги для 35-метровых грузовиков Новости Aвтоновинка Автобизнес Автособытие Автотехнологии Автофанаты Законодательство Тест-драйв Военная техника Подержанные автомобили Вдвое больше дорог для 35-метровых автопоездов: шведы довольны экспериментом с гигантскими фурами 10:00, 19 октября, понедельник В Швеции планируют расширить сеть дорог для 34,5-метровых грузовиков весом 74 тонны, прибавив к разрешенным маршрутам еще 3800 километров. Такое решение приняли после трех лет успешной эксплуатации двойных прицепов, доказавших свою эффективность и безопасность. Как сообщает 40ton.net со ссылкой на дорожную администрацию Швеции (Trafikverket), новый проект поправок к правилам дорожного движения уже прошел этап подготовки и вынесен на официальное обсуждение. Ожидается, что масштабные изменения вступят в силу уже 1 января 2027 года, открыв для сверхтяжелого транспорта новые логистические горизонты. Карта автодорог грузовиков прирастает К этому времени движение автопоездов с двумя полноразмерными прицепами разрешалось на участках общей протяженностью около 6800 километров. В основном это были главные магистрали на юге страны и ключевой северный маршрут к сухопутной границе с Финляндией. Если правительство окончательно утвердит новые нормы, то общая протяженность доступных путей для 74-тонных гигантов возрастет до 10 600 километров. Это даст перевозчикам огромную свободу действий и перекроит всю логистическую карту Скандинавии. Почему двойные прицепы так выгодны У местных чиновников есть железные аргументы в пользу таких транспортных средств. Главное преимущество заключается в бешеной производительности, ведь один тягач забирает груз, для которого раньше требовались две обычные фуры. findings.title: Regulatory Alert: Romania Adopts New Legal Framework for Loading and Unloading Responsibilities in Road Freight Transport
findings.summary: FIATA has been informed by its Member Association, the Freight Forwarders Association of Romania (USER), of an important legislative development in Romania that is expected to have significant implications for road freight transport and logistics operations. On 24 June 2026 , Romania adopted Law No. 100/2026 , establishing, for the first time, a dedicated legal framework governing loading and unloading operations in commercial road freight transport. It will enter into force on 24 July 2026. The new legislation establishes a clear legal framework governing loading and unloading obligations between transport operators, consignors, consignees and freight forwarding intermediaries. It also reinforces the principle that professional drivers should not routinely be required to perform loading and unloading operations. Why was this law introduced? For many years, professional drivers in Romania were frequently required – either contractually or in practice - to carry out loading and unloading operations, despite these activities often falling outside their professional responsibilities. This situation generated several operational and safety concerns, including: increased occupational health and safety risks; longer waiting and driving times; disputes regarding liability for damaged cargo; inconsistencies between contractual obligations and operational practice; reduced efficiency throughout the logistics chain. The new legislation seeks to provide greater legal certainty by establishing a clear framework governing loading and unloading obligations and clarifying the respective responsibilities of the parties involved in road transport operations. findings.title: European HGV Driving Bans: September & October 2026
findings.summary: EU Oversize Weekly · 31 August 2026 European HGV Driving Bans: September & October 2026 DAJC operational reference for published HGV driving bans, weekend and holiday restrictions, seasonal route bans and key regional regimes across Europe for 1 September to 31 October 2026. Scope and how to use this reference This DAJC operational reference covers 1 September to 31 October 2026 and focuses on fixed, pre-published national, public-holiday, weekend, seasonal and major corridor driving restrictions that can affect a goods vehicle or combination above 3.5 tonnes. A critical point: “vehicles above 3.5 t” does not mean every country starts its restriction at 3.5 t. The actual threshold is stated for each regime. Switzerland and Liechtenstein, for example, have restrictions reaching vehicles above 3.5 t, while many other European systems use 7.5 t or 12 t thresholds. All times below are local time in the country or territory concerned . This is not a substitute for road signs, exceptional-transport permits, police instructions or live traffic information. Local access restrictions, LEZ/ZFE rules, construction closures, weather measures, ADR tunnel rules, wartime measures and conditions written into an abnormal-load permit can change independently of a two-month calendar. Quick calendar pattern The most common dates for Sunday restrictions during this period are 6, 13, 20 and 27 September , followed by 4, 11, 18 and 25 October 2026 . The applicable time window, road scope and vehicle threshold vary substantially by country. findings.title: Truck Toll Slovenia: The DarsGo System
findings.summary: Knowledge Base Overview Basics How to Calculate Toll Changes Toll Refunds VAT on tolls How Toll Works Toll Classes & Factors Country Comparison Toll Exemptions Country Profiles Austria Belgium Bulgaria Croatia Czech Republic Denmark France Germany Greece Hungary Italy Luxembourg Netherlands Poland Portugal Romania Serbia Slovakia Slovenia Spain Switzerland Turkey Guides API & MCP Integration Long Routes & Waypoints Truck Toll Slovenia: The DarsGo System Slovenia, as a transit country between Central and Southeast Europe, handles heavy truck traffic. Tolls are collected via the electronic DarsGo system – distance-based across the entire motorway and expressway network. The toll system: DarsGo DarsGo is the national toll system operated by DARS . It works as a free-flow system: vehicles over 3.5 tonnes are automatically detected via OBU or service provider. Charging is in euros . Which roads are tolled? Motorways (A-roads) Expressways (H-roads) Other roads are toll-free. Because Slovenia is compact, toll sections are short – costs often remain manageable. Rate structure: axles, emission class, weight The rate is calculated from three factors: Axle count – factor from 1.0 (2 axles) to 1.9 (5+ axles) Emission class (Euro standard) – factor 1.2 (Euro 0–1) to 0.85 (Euro 6) Vehicle weight – heavier vehicles pay higher base rates The base rate on motorways is €0.168/km . A 40-tonne articulated lorry with 5 axles and Euro 6 pays around €0.27/km – Slovenia is in the European mid-range. Discounts and Concessions Note: User-dependent discounts are the exception in Europe – rates are typically determined solely by vehicle data (weight, axles, Euro/CO₂ class). findings.title: Winter Rules for Trucks in Europe 2026/27: Tyres, Chains and Axle Loads by Country
findings.summary: ← Back to Blog Compliance Winter Rules for Trucks in Europe 2026/27: Tyres, Chains and Axle Loads by Country By Mindaugas Seredis · Oct 18, 2026 What a truck over 3.5 t needs in 16 countries this winter, and why where the load stands matters as much as the tyres. From 1 November, winter equipment stops being optional on a large part of the European road network. Austria requires winter tyres on trucks from 1 November to 15 April. Sweden requires winter tyres on every heavy truck and its trailer from 10 November to 10 April, whatever the weather. The rules are national, and they do not line up. A single run from Kaunas to Stockholm or from Vilnius to Verona can cross four or five different regimes. Fines are the smaller risk. A truck held at a roadside check or turned back before a closed pass loses its delivery slot, and the cost of that lands on whoever planned the trip. Most winter guides stop at tyres and chains. This one also covers the part that belongs to load planning. Traction in snow depends on how much weight sits over the drive axle, and Sweden turns that into a legal requirement during the winter period. A light or badly positioned part load can fail it while the truck is well inside every weight limit. At a glance: winter rules for trucks over 3.5 t Austria, Norway and Sweden apply fixed winter dates to trucks whatever the weather. Elsewhere the rules combine a date window with road conditions or signs, and the Baltic states and Poland set none for heavy vehicles. findings.title: Unmanned border crossings, road transport
findings.summary: Unmanned border crossings, road transport The following list shows the border crossings designated by Swedish Customs for the presentation and arrival notifications for means of transport with an operating authorisation (road traffic). To arrive at an unmanned border crossing, a special decision by the Swedish Customs on exemption from routing and time (operating authorisation) (Chapter 5, Sections 6 and 9 of the Provision on Customs Matters) is required. Here you can read more about operating authorisations for road transport between Sweden and Norway. If the goods are placed in transit, the transit procedure rules will apply. See Transit of goods. Conditions The customs formalities to be completed at the designated border control point depend on which the circumstances of the individual vehicle. The vehicle and the goods carried shall be taken on a route where there is a customs office (customs route) or, by special decision of Customs, via another route or time (Article 135(1) of the Customs Code, Chapter 5, Sections 6 and 9 of the Provisions on Customs Matters). The goods must be brought to a designated border control post (Article 135 of the Customs Code, Chapter 5, sections 6 and 9 of the Provisions on Customs Matters). The arrival of the goods must be notified to Swedish Customs (Article 139(1) of the Customs Code). The goods may be removed from the place of notification only after authorisation from Swedish Customs (Article 139(7) of the Code). Non-Union goods that have been presented to Swedish Customs are in temporary storage (Article 144 of the Code). Non-Union goods must be covered by a temporary storage declaration (Article 145 of the Customs Code, Chapter 6 Section 6, Second Paragraph, and Chapter 6(8) of the Provisions on Customs Matters). findings.title: Operating authorisation for transports between Sweden and Norway
findings.summary: Operating authorisation for transports between Sweden and Norway An operating authorisation gives transport undertakings the option of passing through unmanned border crossings, or manned customs offices outside of opening hours. If you import or export goods from or to Norway, you are normally required to declare your goods at a manned customs office. There are not very many customs offices along the Norwegian border, which may add long transport distances for customs declarations. An operating authorisation (decision to derogate from the route and time) allows transport undertakings to pass through border crossings without a manned customs office. Opening hours for the Swedish and Norwegian customs clearance offices. Conditions To obtain a decision on an operating authorisation, you must carry out regular transport operations that are carried out over a short distance that provides economic and environmental benefits contain uniform goods that are not packaged as general cargo and are not subject to import restrictions where the level of customs duties, taxes and other charges justifies not passing through a manned customs office fulfil the export conditions of the exporting country. In addition to the common criteria, the respective criteria of each country must be met. For Sweden, the following applies: The applicant should have a valid EORI. Apply for an EORI number (in Swedish) . The importer or the representative should be authorised for deferment of payment. The company or representative should submit the customs declarations digitally. Provide the following information in your application: The commodity code of the goods you are transporting The reason for your choice of transport route The name of the designated location at the border crossing point. findings.title: Toll payment tag for heavy vehicles
findings.summary: Toll payment tag for heavy vehicles In Norway, all vehicles with a maximum authorised mass of more than 3,500 kg must have a toll payment tag if they are registered to an enterprise. This also applies to such vehicles registered to a government enterprise, county administration or municipality. If you have a motorhome, SUV or similar with a maximum authorised mass of more than 3,500 kg that you use privately, the vehicle is not subject to this requirement. The legal basis for the mandatory requirement can be found in Sections 13, 31 and 31a of the Road Traffic Act, and in the Regulations relating to the mandatory use of electronic payment unit in motor vehicles above 3,500 kg. To enter into an agreement or to read more about mandatory toll payment tags, see the AutoPASS website. The police, Norwegian Customs and the Norwegian Public Roads Administration are inspection authorities and will carry out roadside inspections of toll tags. What will be inspected? A valid type of tag should be placed inside the windscreen in accordance with instructions The vehicle needs to have a valid toll tag for heavy vehicles. The vehicle needs to have a valid tag with a tag number that is registered to the same vehicle’s number plate/registration number. How is this verified? The Norwegian Public Roads Administration will target heavy vehicles and commercial vehicles and inspect these with regard to the use of mandatory electronic tags. Inspections may take place as random checks, or as part of regular roadside vehicle inspections for other purposes. Omission fines Violation of the regulations will result in a penalty charge of NOK 8,000. If non-compliance is repeated within two years, the fine will be NOK 16,000. Fines must be paid within three weeks even if you appeal , otherwise
findings.searchSummary: In Norway, all vehicles over 3,500 kg registered to an enterprise must have a toll payment tag; violations can result in fines up to NOK 16,000.

findings.title: Road user charges (tolls) for foreign heavy goods vehicles
findings.summary: Road user charges (tolls) for foreign heavy goods vehicles Tolls must be paid for trucks and truck/trailer combinations with a total weight of 12 tonnes or more that are used exclusively for the transport of goods. This information applies only to foreign-registered heavy goods vehicles using the Swedish road network. You can also consult the German organisation AGES for further information on tolls. Eurovignette information (AGES) External link. Other rules apply to Swedish-registered heavy goods vehicles. Tolls for Swedish heavy vehicles (in Swedish) One charge – for two countries On 1 January 1998, Sweden joined the Eurovignette system in which several countries collaborate in the joint collection of tolls for heavy goods vehicles using certain roads. In addition to Sweden, the toll collaboration scheme includes Luxembourg. Tolls paid in one of these countries are also valid for travel in the other country's road network. Vehicles subject to tolls Tolls must be paid for trucks and truck/trailer combinations with a total weight of 12 tonnes or more that are used exclusively for the transport of goods. Toll roads Tolls must be paid on all motorways and the following roads: The E4 between Uppsala and the Finnish border The E10 between Töre and the Norwegian border The E12 between Holmsund and the Norwegian border The E14 between Sundsvall and the Norwegian border The E22 between Karlskrona and Norrköping The E65 between Svedala and Ystad. Payment Tolls must be paid before travel on the toll road starts using the Swedish road network. The German organisation AGES is responsible for selling Eurovignettes on behalf of the Eurovignette countries. Payment can be made at certain fuel stations and forwarding agents, or online at AGES. findings.title: Mandatory AutoPASS Tag for Heavy Vehicles in Norway
findings.summary: Mandatory AutoPASS Tag for Heavy Vehicles in Norway | Fjellinjen - English Jump to main content Mandatory AutoPASS Tag for Heavy Vehicles in Norway All vehicles with a permitted total weight over 3500 kg used for commercial purposes on Norwegian roads must have an active AutoPASS agreement and a toll tag mounted on the windshield. The requirement applies to both Norwegian and foreign vehicles. Drivers who drive without a valid toll tag risk getting a fine. Each year, 5,000 foreign heavy vehicles arrive in Norway for commercial transport without an electronic toll tag. 90 percent of this traffic enters the country via the national borders at Svinesund or Ørje. Foreign drivers will save time by having arranged an AutoPASS agreement and the corresponding toll tag in advance. Nevertheless, most foreign trucks cross the border into Norway without an AutoPASS tag installed in the vehicle. Because the toll tag is mandatory, dedicated toll tag machines have been established at the national border crossings at Svinesund and Ørje. Az MKFE kezdeményezésére» a Közlekedési és Beruházási Minisztérium úgy döntött, hogy részlegesen felfüggeszti a hétvégi kamionstopot 2026. október 22-én és 23-án. A szombat-vasárnapi korlátozás a megszokott rend szerint érvényben marad. A nehéz tehergépjárművek hétvégi forgalomkorlátozása szokás szerint eredetileg 2026. október 22-én, csütörtökön 22 órától október 23-án, pénteken 22 óráig, valamint 2026. október 24-én, szombaton 22 órától október 25-én, vasárnap 22 óráig lett volna érvényben a kamionstop. A hatályos jogszabályok azonban lehetőséget biztosítanak arra, hogy a közlekedési és beruházási miniszter a környezetvédelemért felelős miniszter támogatásával indokolt esetben átmenetileg felfüggessze a korlátozást. A fuvarozói érdekképviseletek kérésére, továbbá mérlegelve a közlekedésbiztonsági és logisztikai szempontokat, a tárcavezető úgy döntött, hogy a kamionstopot 2026. október 22-én, csütörtökön 22:00 óra és 2026. október 23-án, pénteken 06:00 óra között felfüggeszti. (péntek) 6:00 és 22:00 között, október 24. (szombat) 22:00 és 2026. október 25. (vasárnap) 22:00 között. findings.title: Abnormal transports permits
findings.summary: Abnormal transports permit - Economic Development Centre Abnormal transports permits What is an abnormal transport? Who issues permits for abnormal transports in Finland? When permit is required? Applying for abnormal transport permit Permit procedure Prices and effective periods of abnormal transport permit Traffic directing Related links What is an abnormal transport? An abnormal transport is a transport of a vehicle or vehicle combination, having either no load or an indivisible load, which exceeds at least one authorized dimension or weight allowed in normal road traffic in Finland. An indivisible load cannot be divided, for road transport, into two or more loads without unreasonable cost or risk. Due to its weight or dimensions, an indivisible load cannot be transported on any type of vehicle or vehicle combination without exceeding an authorized weight or dimension allowed in normal traffic in Finland. NOTE!! In Finland the authorized dimensions and total weights are partly bigger than in the rest of Europe. See more detailed information in separate appendices about the maximum authorized dimensions and weights allowed in normal traffic in Finland at the end of the page. Who issues permits for abnormal transports in Finland? The Economic Development Centre of Inland Finland is the only organisation that issues permits for abnormal transports in Finland, with the exception of Åland Islands. On Åland, the abnormal transport permit is issued by the provincial government of Åland. When permit is required? Vehicles or vehicle combinations registered in an EU or EEA country Finland allows the same dimensions and weights for all vehicles and vehicle combinations registered in EU and EEA countries as to Finnish vehicles and vehicle combination.
